messages:
anya: heads-up, i'm trying to land a change to the dedicated-gpu autoscaler. current controller primarily uses qps + avg-latency which misses tail p95 spikes. i prototyped a headroom-first approach that uses tail latency signals + soft prewarm credits. sharing quick notes, want feedback.

leo: sounds needed. can you summarize how headroom credits work? we keep hitting p95 regressions on cache-miss bursts.

anya: idea in short: control-plane computes desired soft headroom (n prewarm GPUs) per tenant based on p95 and cache-miss multiplier. it calls operator API SetHeadroom(tenant, count, ttl). operator returns tokens for those soft slots. requests tagged with tokens preferentially route to prewarmed backend. if token consumption exceeds threshold we ConvertToken -> strong reservation.

pranav: ok, two immediate concerns: 1) oscillation if p95 is noisy, 2) fairness when many tenants request prewarm at once.

maria: telemetry question: which p95 source? proxy-level p95 includes network jitter. runtime p95 after kv cache better reflects actual execution latency. we should standardize on runtime p95 and document tag semantics. i'll own the spec if folks want.

leo: for fairness i suggest a soft-queue with randomized backoff and admission windows. also cap per-tenant prewarm to a % of pool to avoid a single tenant hogging credits.

anya: agree on caps. my draft policy config (DSL):
```yaml
autoscale:
  mode: tail_latency
  metric: runtime_p95_ms
  target_p95_ms: 150
  window: 60s
  cooldown: 45s
  soft_headroom: true
  initial_soft_slots: 1
  max_soft_fraction: 0.25
  cache_miss_multiplier: 2.0
  fallback_mode: throughput
```
notes: window uses rolling aggregates; cache miss multiplier increases soft slots when miss_rate > threshold.

pranav: about oscillation mitigation: only scale-up on two consecutive windows of breach, scale-down after 3 cooldowns. also limit growth to +25% nodes/minute. record decision events to kafka for offline analysis.

maria: telemetry reliability: add a guardrail that if telemetry lag >30s (kafka offset), revert to throughput-based autoscale and alert on telemetry.

infra-bot: rollout plan: canary to us-west-2 dedicated pools, feature-flag "headroom-autoscale". alert rule: p95 > target_p95_ms + 20ms for 2m triggers rollback.

leo: operator API shape: SetHeadroom(tenant, count, ttl) -> returns [token...], ListTokens(tenant), ClaimToken(token), ConvertToken(token), ReleaseToken(token). operator implements soft vs strong semantics; control-plane drives intent. operator still owns lifecycle (provision/drain/health).

anya: i want operator minimal: accept intent, allocate containers, hand out tokens. control-plane handles billing/decisions. operator should expose metrics about soft-slot usage, conversions, and ttl expiries.

dave: cost/accounting: prewarm credits must be metered. either bill discounted prewarm minute or tag usage for chargeback. otherwise customers will game it.

pranav: also need a tie-breaker when multiple tenants exceed headroom simultaneously: prioritize by SLA tier, then by recent usage, then randomized. implement soft jitter on TTL to avoid stampedes.

maria: one more: define "conversion" threshold. e.g., token consumed > 80% of its window -> convert to strong. that avoids churning tokens.

leo: and add safety caps: global pool-level soft headroom cap and emergency drain that falls back to throughput routing if operator can't satisfy headroom requests.

anya: action items: 1) i'll draft RFC that defines API + policy DSL + rollout plan. 2) leo will help on proto/operator shim. 3) maria will write telemetry spec. 4) pranav will implement autoscaler smoothing + decision events. 5) infra-bot will run canary. i'll open RFC PR later today and link this thread.

anya: anyone want to co-author the RFC?

leo: i'll co-author the proto/operator sections.

maria: i'll co-review telemetry and tagging.

pranav: i'll co-review autoscaler logic.

anya: great. i'll ping again with PR link. :thumbsup:
